recommendation: Check for an updated, multi-threaded version of the app; setting its process priority to Below Normal can reduce its impact on the rest of the system.

recommendation: From Recovery > Command Prompt run 'bootrec /rebuildbcd'; if it finds no Windows installations, rebuild manually with 'bcdboot C:\Windows'.

recommendation: Rebuild the boot files from Recovery > Command Prompt with 'bootrec /rebuildbcd' followed by 'bcdboot C:\Windows /s S: /f UEFI' (where S: is the EFI system partition).

recommendation: In an elevated prompt run 'diskpart', 'select disk 1', then 'attributes disk clear readonly'; check for a physical write-protect switch if it's an SD card or USB drive.

summary: The spooler was running but in a stuck state, showing the printer offline. Restarting the Print Spooler cleared the stuck status and the printer returned to Normal.

recommendation: Right-click the app's .exe > Properties > Compatibility > Change high DPI settings > 'Override' and pick 'System (Enhanced)'.

recommendation: Run the update as the SYSTEM context does (no manual elevation fixes this): restore default ACLs with 'icacls C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution /reset /t', temporarily disable third-party antivirus, and retry.

goal: An app fails with error 0x80004005 'Unspecified error' when accessing a network share
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context

Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x80004005 is a catch-all failure, but paired with a network share it almost always maps to an SMB authentication/protocol negotiation failure -- here the client had insecure guest auth disabled while the share only allows guest access.
recommendation: The secure fix is enabling authenticated access on the share (add a real user account on the NAS/server); enabling insecure guest logons on the client works but reintroduces a security risk.

plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context

recommendation: Boot to Recovery and run 'sfc /scannow /offbootdir=C:\ /offwindir=C:\Windows' followed by 'DISM /Image:C:\ /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth'; if a third-party credential/logon tool was recently installed, uninstall it from Safe Mode.

summary: 0x80070490 indicates a corrupted entry in the component-based servicing (CBS) store or a damaged system file the update depends on -- the update engine literally can't find a manifest element it expects.
recommendation: Run DISM RestoreHealth then SFC (in that order), reboot, and retry the update; if it still fails, install the update manually from the Microsoft Update Catalog.

goal: MSI installer fails with error 1603 'A fatal error occurred during installation'

recommendation: Re-run with verbose logging ('msiexec /i app.msi /L*v log.txt') to confirm the failing action, clear the target folder's lock/permission problem, ensure no other MSI is in progress, and retry.

goal: Enabling .NET Framework 3.5 fails with error 0x800F081F 'source files could not be found'
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x800F081F means the on-demand feature payload isn't in the local component store and Windows couldn't fetch it (commonly blocked by WSUS policy that redirects feature-on-demand requests away from Windows Update).
recommendation: Enable it with an explicit source from matching install media: 'DISM /Online /Enable-Feature /FeatureName:NetFx3 /All /Source:D:\sources\sxs /LimitAccess', or have IT enable the 'Specify settings for optional component installation' GPO to allow direct Windows Update fetch.

goal: Windows 10 to 11 feature update fails with 0xC1900101 and rolls back

recommendation: Update or temporarily uninstall the specific driver/security product named in setuperr.log, disconnect nonessential peripherals, and retry the feature update; reinstall the software afterward.

goal: Installing from a USB/ISO fails with error 0x80070570 'The file or directory is corrupted and unreadable'

recommendation: Re-download the ISO and re-create the USB with the official Media Creation Tool; if a verified-good USB still throws 0x80070570, run MemTest86 because failing RAM produces this same error.

recommendation: Stop wuauserv/bits/cryptsvc, rename both 'SoftwareDistribution' and 'System32\catroot2', restart the services, and re-check for updates so everything re-downloads cleanly.

recommendation: Report to IT: the WsusPool IIS application pool on the WSUS server needs restarting (and usually a private-memory limit increase to stop it recycling under load).

recommendation: Update or uninstall the software owning the faulting DLL (screen-overlay/RGB/antivirus injectors are common); if unclear, run the app with overlays disabled to confirm.

recommendation: Update the Wi-Fi adapter driver (the usual culprit for 0x9F on laptops), and as a stopgap disable 'Allow the computer to turn off this device' on that adapter so suspend doesn't hang on it.

recommendation: Run Windows Memory Diagnostic/MemTest86; set both DIMMs to the same (lower) speed in BIOS or replace the mismatched kit with a matched pair.

recommendation: Start W32Time and resync ('Start-Service W32Time; w32tm /resync'); with a correct clock the TLS errors disappear. If the clock drifts again after shutdowns, replace the CMOS battery.

recommendation: Report to IT that port 1688 to the KMS host is blocked from this subnet (or the KMS host is down); once reachable, activate immediately with 'slmgr /ato'.

goal: Service operations fail with 0x800706BA 'The RPC server is unavailable' against a remote machine

recommendation: Enable the 'Remote Service Management' / 'Windows Management Instrumentation' firewall rule groups on the remote host (or the equivalent GPO), which open TCP 135 plus the dynamic RPC range.

recommendation: On the target machine, enable 'File and Printer Sharing' in the firewall for the correct network profile, and confirm the 'Server' (LanmanServer) service is running.

goal: Windows installation fails with 0x80300024 'Windows is unable to install to the selected location'

recommendation: Patch the unpatched side (preferred) with current Windows updates; only as a temporary bridge, relax enforcement via the 'Encryption Oracle Remediation' GPO, and revert once both sides are patched.

recommendation: Stop WSearch, delete the search Data folder contents so the index rebuilds from scratch, restart the service, and exclude the search database path from cleanup tools.

recommendation: Replace mapped drive letters with full UNC paths in the script, and set the task's 'Start in' directory explicitly; grant the run-as account NTFS access to the UNC target.

goal: Printing fails with error 0x0000011B on a shared network printer

recommendation: Update both client and print server fully with current Windows updates, then remove and re-add the printer connection; avoid registry workarounds that disable RPC authentication hardening.

goal: Windows Backup (wbadmin) fails with 0x8078002A on a large external drive
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context

Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x8078002A occurs when block-level backup hits a target using 4K-native sectors that the backup engine can't handle -- the external drive reports 4096-byte logical sectors, which wbadmin's VHD format doesn't support.
recommendation: Use a 512-byte-emulation (512e) drive as the backup target, check the drive vendor's tool for a sector-emulation mode, or switch to File History/a third-party imaging tool that supports 4Kn targets.

goal: Domain join fails with error 0x6D9 'There are no more endpoints available from the endpoint mapper'
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.command: Clear-DnsClientCache; Measure-Command { Resolve-DnsName microsoft.com } | Select-Object TotalMilliseconds

summary: DNS lookups were taking ~840 ms on the ISP resolver. Switching to Cloudflare/Google DNS and flushing the cache cut resolution to ~28 ms.

plan: Start bthserv

steps.stderr: Service 'Bluetooth Support Service (bthserv)' cannot be started due to the following error: Access is denied.

summary: The Bluetooth Support Service is stopped and starting it failed with Access Denied, meaning the current session lacks the rights to control the service.

Disable radio power saving
Verify device

steps.command: Get-PnpDevice -Class Bluetooth | Where-Object FriendlyName -like '*Intel*' | Select-Object Status, InstanceId

recommendation: If drops return, update the Intel Bluetooth driver and disable USB selective suspend.

plan: Avoid mass destructive removal
Restart the stack instead

steps.reason: Irreversible or session-disrupting operation — needs a human decision.

summary: Bulk-removing all Bluetooth PnP devices was blocked as too disruptive (it can remove the radio itself). Restarting the Bluetooth service refreshed the stack, which resolves most pairing glitches without removing hardware.
recommendation: Remove only the specific problem device from Settings > Bluetooth, then re-pair it.

summary: The Bluetooth audio endpoint is in an Error state, so Windows can't route sound to it or set it as default. This is usually a Bluetooth audio driver problem.
recommendation: Remove the device, reboot, re-pair it; if the endpoint still errors, update the Bluetooth audio driver from the laptop vendor.

plan: Check service startup type
Set it to automatic
Verify
summary: The Bluetooth service was set to Manual, so it didn't always start at boot. Setting it to Automatic keeps Bluetooth on across restarts.

goal: A process is pinned at 100% CPU and I can't end it
plan: Find the process
Attempt to stop it

steps.stderr: Stop-Process : Cannot stop process 'MsMpEng (3120)' because of the following error: Access is denied.

recommendation: Don't force-kill Defender. Let the scan finish, or add large dev folders to Defender exclusions to reduce its CPU.

goal: Fans always loud, System process using high CPU

Advise driver check

steps.stderr: Stop-Process : Cannot stop process 'System (4)' Access is denied.

summary: High CPU is under the System process (PID 4), which hosts kernel/driver threads and cannot be killed. Sustained high System CPU almost always means a misbehaving driver, not a runaway app.
recommendation: Update chipset, storage and network drivers; use 'Reliability Monitor' or a tool like LatencyMon to pinpoint the driver.

plan: Confirm folder
Take ownership
summary: The folder is owned by TrustedInstaller, so taking ownership failed without elevation. This is a permissions issue, not a missing folder.
recommendation: Relaunch as Administrator, then: takeown /f "C:\Program Files\OldApp" /r /d y && icacls "C:\Program Files\OldApp" /grant administrators:F /t, then delete.

plan: Refuse deleting system roots

recommendation: Delete only C:\Temp\build-cache; never remove C:\Windows or drive roots.

Run SFC in case Office files are damaged

steps.stdout: Windows Resource Protection could not perform the requested operation.

recommendation: Open Word > File > Open > pick the file > arrow next to Open > 'Open and Repair'. Also try a File History / OneDrive previous version.

steps.stderr: Set-NetFirewallProfile : Access is denied. (Exception from HRESULT: 0x80070005)

Attempt to stop it

recommendation: Run a Microsoft Defender Offline scan (reboots into a clean environment) to remove it, since it can't be stopped from the running session.

recommendation: Re-run Windows Update; delete SoftwareDistribution.old once updates succeed.
